france24fr.description: Plusieurs grandes entreprises chinoises ont rompu leur collaboration avec Kylian Mbappé. Le joueur a présenté ses excuses, invoquant "un profond respect pour le peuple chinois et son histoire".

france24fr.title: Élections en Israël : retrouvez l'intégralité du discours de Benjamin Netanyahu
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre israélien, Benjamin Netanyahu, dont le camp est donné au coude-à-coude avec celui de l'opposition dans les sondages de sortie des urnes, a appelé mercredi à la formation d'un gouvernement "de droite" et "fort".

france24fr.title: Tennis : fin d'une longue carrière pour le Suisse Stan Wawrinka, battu au 1er tour à Bâle
france24fr.description: Battu mardi à Bâle par le Tchèque Jiri Lehecka, le Suisse Stan Wawrinka, triple vainqueur en Grand Chelem, quitte le circuit après 16 titres et une longue carrière. Ancien N.3 mondial, il était l’un des rares joueurs à avoir contesté l’emprise de Federer, Nadal et Djokovic.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Israël : le camp de Netanyahu en tête, mais sans majorité
france24fr.description: Aucune majorité parlementaire ne se dessine en Israël après le dépouillement de plus de la moitié des suffrages. Le Premier ministre sortant Benjamin Netanyahu arrive légèrement en tête, mais ni lui ni son rival Gadi Eisenkot n'obtiennent le nombre de sièges nécessaires à la formation d'une majorité. Ils se sont tous deux dits mercredi prêts à former un gouvernement. Les partis vont désormais se lancer dans des semaines d'intenses tractations pour tenter de former une coalition gouvernementale.

Élections en Israël : Gadi Eisenkot peut-il battre Benjamin Netanyahu ?
france24fr.description: Quelque sept millions d'Israéliens ont été appelés aux urnes pour les élections législatives – les premières depuis les attaques du Hamas le 7 octobre 2023. Ce mardi est férié dans le pays. Les deux blocs, celui du Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu, et celui de l'opposition emmené par l'ancien chef d'état-major Gadi Eisenkot, sont au coude-à-coude dans les sondages.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : le Danemark reproche à la Finlande et à la Norvège d'avoir joué "solo" en appelant Poutine
france24fr.description: Le président finlandais Alexander Stubb et le Premier ministre norvégien Jonas Gahr Store se sont entretenus mardi par téléphone avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine pour ouvrir un "canal de communication" avec le Kremlin. La Première ministre danoise, Mette Frederiksen, s’est dite "sceptique" quant à l’initiative et a reproché à ses voisins de l'avoir joué "solo".

france24fr.title: 🔴 Législatives israéliennes en direct : la Commission électorale rejette la demande du Likoud de prolonger le vote
Élections en Serbie : "La mobilisation contre la fraude a sûrement eu un impact sur les résultats"
france24fr.description: Le mouvement de contestation mené par les étudiants en Serbie a remporté dimanche une victoire historique aux élections législatives, battant le parti du président démissionnaire Aleksandar Vucic. Les soutiens de la liste étudiante expliquent comment ils se sont massivement mobilisés afin d’empêcher les fraudes électorales, avant et pendant le scrutin.

france24fr.title: Flavio Bolsonaro a fui le Brésil malgré l'annulation de ses passeports
france24fr.description: Deux jours après sa défaite à la présidentielle, le sénateur ultraconservateur Flavio Bolsonaro a fui le Brésil en passant par l'Argentine puis l'Equateur, après avoir refusé de se conformer à une décision de la Cour suprême lui ordonnant de remettre ses passeports. Le gouvernement américain va lui délivrer un visa.

france24fr.title: Serbie : l'ex-dirigeant Aleksandar Vucic va-t-il vraiment manquer à la Russie ?
france24fr.description: Considéré comme l’un des principaux soutiens de la Russie en Europe, le dirigeant nationaliste serbe Aleksandar Vucic a perdu, dimanche, les élections législatives face au mouvement étudiant. Mais il est encore trop tôt pour dire que la Serbie va couper les ponts avec Moscou. Explications.

france24fr.title: Cessez-le-feu à Olechky pour faciliter l'acheminement d'aide humanitaire
france24fr.description: Washington avait choisi de faire annoncer vendredi par la première dame américaine, Melania Trump, cette trêve obtenue à Olechky pour faciliter l'acheminement d'aide humanitaire et l'évacuation d'habitants, la Russie refusant un cessez-le-feu généralisé.

france24fr.description: Antoine Mariotti, notre chroniqueur international, analyse la situation.

france24fr.title: Chine : Mbappé s'excuse après être accusé d'offense aux sentiments nationaux
france24fr.description: La superstar française Kylian Mbappé a présenté "ses excuses" et s'est dit "sincèrement désolé" après avoir fait face à une levée de boucliers et l'annulation de contrats publicitaires en Chine à la suite de la diffusion en ligne d'une vidéo dans laquelle il semble plaisanter à propos de l'ancien dirigeant historique Mao Zedong.

observador.description: Seguro quer diálogo, mas que não lhe arranjem problemas. Montenegro não recua na habitação e o Ministério está focado nos professores nas escolas. Já Flávio Bolsonaro perdeu a eleição e fugiu ilegal.

observador.title: "Netanyahu é o grande sobrevivente da política israelita"
observador.description: Para o historiador Bruno Cardoso Reis, Israel continua dramaticamente dividido e Netanyahu volta a provar que é o grande sobrevivente da política, capaz de superar todos os sobressaltos desta eleição.

observador.title: Argentina confirma que Flávio Bolsonaro entrou no país
observador.description: Senador saiu do Brasil com a família durante a noite pela fronteira terrestre para a Argentina. Voaram para o Equador e, ao que tudo indica, irão para os EUA. Trump já disse que serão bem-vindos.

observador.title: Parlamento continua debate e vota a proposta do OE 2027
observador.description: É o segundo dia de debate do Orçamento do Estado para o próximo ano. Proposta é votada hoje na generalidade e tem já aprovação garantida.

observador.title: 7h. Argentina confirma que Flávio Bolsonaro entrou no país

observador.title: Trump deixa no ar possibilidade de novo ataque ao Irão
observador.description: O Presidente dos EUA foi questionado sobre as intenções de um novo ataque ao Irão. "Não posso dizer, mas tudo é possível", disse.

observador.title: Trump elimina regulamentação sobre emissões de metano
observador.description: Trump garantiu que a medida permitirá poupar 45 mil milhões de dólares, desbloquear grandes quantidades de gás natural do Texas e produzir 210 milhões de barris adicionais de petróleo.

observador.title: Netanyahu à frente sem maioria, árabes aumentam votação

nzz.title: Die linke Heilsbringerin: Isabella Weber will mit Preiskontrollen gegen Rechtsextreme ankämpfen
nzz.description: Mit ihrem Buch «Antifaschistische Wirtschaftspolitik» hat die deutsche Ökonomin einen Bestseller gelandet. Ihr Plan für tiefere Lebenshaltungskosten trifft den Nerv der Zeit. Er droht aber genau in den Autoritarismus zu führen, den sie verhindern will.

Gleichzeitig gewinnen im demokratischen Lager muslimische Stimmen in entscheidenden Swing States an Gewicht. Im Podcast analysiert der Politikwissenschafter Stephan Bierling diese Dynamik.

spiegel.description: In Frankreich gab es schwere Ausschreitungen und Plünderungen. Nun beziffert die französische Handelskammer erstmals das Ausmaß der Einbußen und listet auf, wie viele Geschäfte beschädigt wurden.

phys-org.title: Digital tools and 3D printing emerge as key themes in circular economy research
phys-org.description: A review of the research literature spanning the years 2020 to 2026 has found that digital technologies, additive manufacturing and resource recovery are major themes in the transition toward a sustainable, circular economy. The work, published in the International Journal of Services and Operations Management, highlights the need for more cooperation between businesses and other stakeholders and for better governmental policies to ease the transition.

phys-org.title: New election forecast updates predictions every 10 minutes
phys-org.description: From Alaska to Texas, the battle for control of the U.S. Senate is unfolding across 35 races. And a new Northwestern University election model is tracking them all—every 10 minutes.

phys-org.title: Halloween meets history in many ghostly tourism attractions. Is this a problem?
phys-org.description: Halloween, the fall holiday and $13.5 billion industry, lurks around the corner.

phys-org.title: Brambles are a problem weed in South Africa, but researchers are closer to finding a natural enemy to manage them
phys-org.description: Invasive alien brambles have been spreading across South Africa since the early 1900s, having come from North America and Europe. All brambles fall within the genus Rubus. Their common names in South Africa are braam (Afrikaans), ijingijolo (isiZulu) and monoko-metsi (seSotho).

phys-org.title: Researchers produce urea in the field using system powered by biobatteries and solar energy
phys-org.description: The CONFETI project, coordinated by the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB), has concluded three years of research with the commissioning of a pilot system capable of producing urea, a nitrogen fertilizer widely used in agriculture, directly in the field using renewable energy. This fertilizer is produced from carbon dioxide (CO₂) and nitrates in an electrochemical reactor powered by energy from biobatteries and solar panels.

phys-org.title: Researchers discover why some frogs have escaped the current amphibian mass extinction
phys-org.description: Amphibians are the most threatened vertebrates on Earth, with 41% of species facing extinction. In the highlands of Central and South America, a killer fungus has wiped out much of the once-abundant amphibian diversity. Yet in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, an isolated mountain range in northern Colombia, amphibians still thrive. The mountain range is home to a remarkable amphibian community of at least 48 species, including 25 found nowhere else on the planet.

phys-org.title: Injuries matter less in the NFL than you think
phys-org.description: New research from Northwestern's Kellogg School of Management finds that injury matters less in the NFL than is often assumed. With the exception of highly paid quarterbacks, losing players—even the high-dollar ones—to injury is not as fatal to a team's success as one might think.

phys-org.title: Report indicates water, food and power at risk by strong El Niño
phys-org.description: Rainfall reductions of up to 80% and torrential precipitation leading to severe flooding and landslides are the expected consequences across different areas of Latin America and the Caribbean from the impact of the El Niño phenomenon in 2027, according to a report co-authored by the General Secretariat of the Organization of American States (OAS), which urges member states to strengthen prevention and preparedness during the final months of 2026.

phys-org.title: Cost overruns aren't just due to incompetence, bureaucracy and bad faith
phys-org.description: Nine out of 10 major transportation projects go over their initial budget. This isn't always because of incompetence.

phys-org.title: Punishment alone won't help gang‑involved teens—a former child soldier explains why
phys-org.description: When Americans hear of child soldiers, they may imagine tragic images of children wielding rifles on distant battlefields.

phys-org.title: Climate health harms outpace action, prompting calls for global health emergency
phys-org.description: The 2026 Report of The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change finds that many of the health risks and harms of climate change grew faster in the decade since the Paris Agreement was introduced (2016–2025) than in the decade before it (2006–2015).

phys-org.title: Decoding the loopy physics of hula hooping with high-tech earthquake sensors
phys-org.description: Hula hooping may be literal child's play, but as it turns out, the physics behind the gym-class staple is so complicated that scientists have spent decades trying to understand how the hula hoop defies gravity.

phys-org.title: We studied 1,584 data centers—and found the buildings full of machines are tied to modest local job growth
phys-org.description: Data centers require enormous investments: land, buildings, computer equipment and power infrastructure. Yet, once they're up and running, they tend to employ no more than a few dozen people in occupations such as IT technicians, engineers and security guards. With billions of dollars flowing into new data centers across the United States, communities are asking what they will get in return.

phys-org.title: Biodiversity hotspots in southwestern Germany are losing their species richness
phys-org.description: Climate change and shifts in land use are affecting habitats and, consequently, plant diversity. To better understand the consequences of these developments, long-term and comprehensive data are essential. phys-org.title: The way Earth's 'thermostat' works may have changed during Pangea era
phys-org.description: Life arose on Earth at least 3.5 billion years ago, and our planet has remained habitable ever since—not too hot, not too cold. These life-sustaining conditions are possible in part thanks to a built-in, carbon cycle–based climate "thermostat" that controls the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

phys-org.title: Identical vesicles, different behaviors: Model reveals how spontaneous asymmetry gives rise to lifelike behavior
phys-org.description: In nonreciprocal active matter, agents act differently on each other, seemingly in violation of Newton's third law. This principle can result in various active matter traits, such as self-propulsion, molecular regulation and collective motion.

phys-org.description: It's Halloween night. Someone has dared you to turn off the lights and stand in front of the mirror. The rules are simple: Stare into your reflection and say her name three times.

undark.title: Podcast: The Entanglements Series Finale
undark.description: Welcome to the last installment of Entanglements, at least for the foreseeable future. In this final episode, hosts Brooke Borel and Anna Rothschild are joined by Undark editor-in-chief Tom Zeller Jr. to talk about the show’s successes, failures, and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

proj-syn.description: Brazil’s renewed democratic confidence must now be matched by institutional and structural reforms and a willingness to build coalitions beyond the left. Recent democratic outcomes in Hungary and Serbia offer useful lessons.

proj-syn.title: Another Crash Landing for Brazil’s Economy?
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s floating exchange rate, high foreign-exchange reserves, strong commodity exports, and debt denominated predominantly in its own currency reduce its exposure to a balance-of-payments crisis. Nonetheless, continued fiscal deterioration under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will carry high domestic costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Make-or-Break Moment Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has not only abandoned Ukraine and America’s European allies, but has increasingly sided with Russian President Vladimir Putin. To preserve their sovereignty, Europeans must remain united in the face of outside pressure, which in turn requires managing political threats from within their borders.

proj-syn.title: Middle Powers Can Lead on AI Safety
proj-syn.description: With the United States showing no interest in regulating AI, middle powers have an opportunity to take the lead on governance. By banding together, these countries could condition market access on meeting a common set of safety requirements and explore joint investment in technical capacity.

proj-syn.title: Lula Killed the Donroe Doctrine
proj-syn.description: In attempting to disentangle the United States from the rest of the world and retreat into a seemingly controllable hemispheric stronghold, Donald Trump's Latin America strategy had fared better than the rest of his foreign policy. But following a defeat for the far right in Brazil, his project now looks dead in the water.

proj-syn.title: The Wrong Way to Compare Economic Size
proj-syn.description: At the European Central Bank’s annual research conference, Paul Krugman concluded that, when it comes to “weaponized interdependence,” the EU is more powerful than both the US and China. But his reliance on PPP-adjusted GDP as a way to smooth out the volatility of nominal exchange rates ignores the even greater swings in PPP data.

proj-syn.title: Public Control for a Purposeful Economy
proj-syn.description: As more governments recognize the need for greater public control over economic outcomes, they must be careful to define the concept well. What ultimately matters is not ownership, but the state’s capacity to steer economic activity toward strategic objectives in the service of the common good.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Sustainable Livelihoods From the Ground Up
proj-syn.description: In regions where economic activity has long revolved around fossil-fuel extraction, ensuring a just transition requires developing alternative livelihoods that account for each community’s specific needs. Regional endowment funds could be a useful vehicle for funding these local initiatives.

proj-syn.title: The Specter of an AI-Driven Slowdown
proj-syn.description: The rush to finance AI infrastructure is driving up borrowing costs just as governments grapple with mounting debt and persistent fiscal deficits. If the AI investment boom falters, falling valuations could choke off financing, with little room for fiscal and monetary policy to cushion the economic shock.

proj-syn.title: Is a Chinese Implosion Looming?
proj-syn.description: If current trends continue, the Chinese state will find itself exposed to a political succession crisis, a weakening economy, and a lack of resources to exercise power domestically and project it externally. It would be a perfect storm, with far-reaching global repercussions.

proj-syn.title: PS Events: Reinventing Europe – Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
proj-syn.description: When we talk about "reinvention" we often overlook what works, noted WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala in her closing keynote. This is true of the global trading system, which has proven surprisingly resilient in recent years, and of the European economy, which might not have a tech giant to rival those in the US or China, but remains a global trade powerhouse and a leader in science and research. While Europe has much to do to improve its external competitiveness, it must not ac

proj-syn.title: Who Pays the Fiscal Watchdogs?
proj-syn.description: Civil-society oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance, because it enables independent scrutiny long before a default. But given that a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it, global decision-makers must do so using agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments.

proj-syn.title: How to Help Left-Behind Regions
proj-syn.description: Pouring public investment into poorer towns and cities might be politically beneficial, but the economic returns of indiscriminate largesse would be limited. A better approach would concentrate investment in areas with the potential to become high-productivity hubs, such as large peripheral cities.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: A Competitive Europe Must Be Climate-Resilient
proj-syn.description: Extreme weather and climate-related events caused €822 billion in economic losses across the European Union between 1980 and 2024, with a quarter of the losses occurring just in the last five years. The consequences for Europe’s competitiveness and economic security are clear—and so is the appropriate response.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Prepare for the Worst
proj-syn.description: Those seeking to weaken the EU’s supranational foundations are already preparing their radical schemes, like the “new deal for Europe” that Germany's Alternative für Deutschland recently presented in the European Parliament. The pro-EU camp must be prepared with new political strategies and institutional arrangements.

proj-syn.title: Nature Can’t Wait
proj-syn.description: Although the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine are spurring governments to increase spending on defense and focus more on economic growth, it would be a mistake to postpone investments designed to protect nature. In fact, meeting internationally agreed targets could add up to $450 billion to annual global GDP by 2050.

proj-syn.description: Argentine President Javier Milei may currently be a lynchpin in US President Donald Trump’s geoeconomic vision for Latin America; but he could soon become its weak link. With elections coming next year, he has achieved an economic recovery and relative price stability by driving millions of his people into destitution.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows Q3 Robotics Startup Funding Jumps 185% As US And China Lead Physical AI Push
crunchbase.description: Venture funding to robotics startups has soared in 2026, with the bulk of investment going to companies based in China and the U.S., Crunchbase data shows. All told, global venture funding to robotics startups totaled $9.9 billion in Q3, more than double the $4.3 billion invested in Q3 2025, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: Your AI Agents Need A Chief Operating Officer, Too
crunchbase.description: Scaling AI agents requires treating them like employees in regulated roles, with written rules, clearly defined responsibilities and a named human manager accountable for their performance. Guest author Rick Folgmann, COO at Get Covered, tells companies they should start with tasks governed by established rules, adjust autonomy to each workflow’s risks, and regularly review results before expanding agents’ authority.

crunchbase.title: Some Observations About Anthropic’s IPO Filing
crunchbase.description: In an S-1 filing today preceding what could be the largest IPO ever, Anthropic laid out extensive new details about its earnings, growth, key stakeholders and the risks it faces going forward. Clocking in at 335 pages, the document wasn’t exactly light reading. However, in a preliminary once-over, we highlight some of the more intriguing disclosures.

crunchbase.title: When Traction Becomes Personal Exposure: What The Joonko Guilty Plea Means For Founders
crunchbase.description: False claims about customers, revenue and AI capabilities can expose founders to personal securities-fraud liability, with D&O insurance offering limited protection against established misconduct. Guest author Kyle Jeziorski of Founder Shield shares three policy provisions that need close attention from founders.

crunchbase.title: California Startups Have Raised More So Far In 2026 Than The Entire US Ever Has In A Single Year
crunchbase.description: California companies have scooped up more than three-fourths of all U.S. startup funding this year. That, per Crunchbase data, is an apparent record share. And keep in mind: This year still has a couple months left.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
crunchbase.description: It was another interesting week for AI-related startup funding, with a number of large rounds and quirky companies. The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.

crunchbase.title: Protecting Trade Secrets In The Age Of AI
crunchbase.description: AI agents create new trade secret risks by allowing employees to access expertise or inadvertently expose proprietary information through personal devices. In this guest commentary, Seth Kugler, a partner at Grellas Shah LLP, warns companies that they should adopt strict AI policies, restrict data access on unmanaged devices, update confidentiality agreements, and act immediately when misuse is suspected.

crunchbase.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: Robot Training, Space Lasers And Greener Cement
crunchbase.description: From teaching robots to do everyday household chores to using lasers to track satellites in space, this month's crop of interesting startup deals spans some decidedly different corners of tech.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Slingshot Raises $27M In Seed Funding To Build An Insurer For Those Small Policies Sold At Checkout
crunchbase.description: Slingshot Insurance, a Minneapolis-based AI-native embedded insurance startup, is emerging from stealth with $27 million in a seed funding round co-led by Rally Ventures and Skyward Group, it tells Crunchbase News exclusively.

crunchbase.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
crunchbase.description: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.
